title: Irelia VS Sivir Aurora: a Grand Final lesson in breaking Aurora tempo
result: EDG Rico1997 defeats TSS SouledOut 2-0 and wins the Sydney Regional Qualifier.

chapters.title: Irelia player view
points: Game 1 shows why Adaptatron is more than a tech card: once it is protected and moved cleanly, the Aurora player loses the turn where Dazzling Aurora is supposed to convert mana into inevitability.

Rico wins by asking smaller questions first. Scuttle Crab and Tideturner make the Sivir hand visible, Ride the Wind changes the battlefield math, and the Irelia side keeps pressure without walking into a full Elder Dragon reset.

Game 2 is the important teaching game. Not So Fast protects Adaptatron, denies the most explosive Elder Dragon and Flurry of Blades line, and lets Rico finish before SouledOut can turn a single Aurora trigger into a second setup turn.

chapters.title: Sivir Aurora player view
points: SouledOut's list is built to make Dazzling Aurora and Elder Dragon the biggest questions on the table, but the finals show that the deck still needs a clean first trigger window.

The Irelia side does not have to beat every large card directly. It can make the Aurora turn awkward by moving pressure, forcing interaction before the big reveal, and saving hard answers for the exact turn that matters.

For Sivir players, the review target is sequencing: protect the Aurora turn, count whether Adaptatron must be answered before the reveal, and do not let Flurry of Blades or Elder Dragon become the only visible plan.
